attack_path_facts.title: Mistral model resolution lacks response-body and read-time bounds

affected_locations.label: model-list GET and full JSON materialization

attack_steps: The operator uses the default mutable Mistral model alias in an approved online workflow.
KCS performs the authenticated model-list request before OCR.
The configured remote endpoint, proxy, or intermediary slow-streams or returns an oversized or compressed model-list body.
KCS reads, decompresses, and fully materializes the JSON without a read or overall deadline or byte ceiling before family and stability filtering, hanging the command or consuming substantial memory.
assumptions: The mutable default alias is used rather than a fixed immutable model.
An online Mistral operation is authorized and a connected remote peer behaves maliciously or incorrectly.
attack_path_facts.context: This is a distinct pre-OCR remote availability path. The provider destination is selected by the operator, but remote response behavior is explicitly untrusted in the threat model.
attack_path_facts.in_scope: yes; remote model-catalog timing and body bounds fall under the adapter and bounded-processing invariants I3, I6, and I12
attack_path_facts.exposure: outbound remote model-list request after online-adapter authorization; no inbound listener
attack_path_facts.identity: KCS uses the victim OS identity and configured Mistral credential; the connected peer controls response timing and bytes
attack_path_facts.cross_boundary: yes; remote response behavior crosses the adapter boundary into synchronous victim-process time and memory consumption
attack_path_facts.preconditions: plausible: default mutable alias, approved online use, and a malicious, compromised, or faulty connected endpoint or intermediary
attack_path_facts.attacker_control: yes; the remote peer controls header/body timing and compressed or uncompressed model-list size
attack_path_facts.category: remote response resource exhaustion / missing deadline (CWE-400, CWE-770)
mitigations: A fixed immutable model bypasses model-list resolution.
Credentials, HTTP status mapping, JSON validity, and post-parse family/stability filters remain enforced.
attack_path_facts.impact_surface: command availability and transient process memory/CPU before OCR
attack_path_facts.target_reach: one online Mistral command and selected scope per malicious catalog response
secrets_references: The configured Mistral API credential is attached to the already approved model-list request; no unintended recipient was established.
counterevidence: Fixed model pins avoid the vulnerable request.
Connect time is bounded and semantic model filtering prevents adoption of unrelated IDs, but both controls fail to bound a connected peer's read or body.
blindspots: No loopback timing or body-size measurement was retained; exact resource thresholds remain unknown.
controls: HTTP, JSON, model-family, and stability validation after materialization
attack_path_facts.rationale: The connected remote peer is a realistic in-scope attacker source on the default approved path. Impact is local availability rather than compromise, and the required matrix maps medium impact plus high likelihood to medium.
